hardware_summary: As-designed replica of Coral Sul FLNG's topsides: aeroderivative-gas-turbine-driven turbo-compression trains (mechanical drive, refrigeration) plus separate aeroderivative-gas-turbine-driven turbo-generation units (electric generators) — vendor/model not yet separately announced for this hull.
fuel_basis: Same feed-gas-fired aeroderivative gas turbines as the sister vessel Coral Sul FLNG (see Coral South FLNG Terminal entry, this shard); TechnipFMC states it is replicating that design.
captive_summary: Coral North (vessel 'Coral Norte', launched Jan 2026 at Samsung Heavy's Geoje yard) is Eni's second Coral-field FLNG, EPCIC'd by the same Technip Energies/JGC/Samsung Heavy (TJS-style) consortium that built Coral Sul. TechnipFMC's own release says it will 'leverage our experience gained from the successful delivery of Coral South... by replicating our proven playbook.' Coral Sul's confirmed design carries both mechanical-drive refrigeration turbines and dedicated turbo-generation power units (see next entry), so the as-designed captive power finding on this proposed/pre-startup (targeted 2028) sister project is a YES on design, not yet independently confirmed equipment-by-equipment.
mechanical_drive_note: Not separately confirmed for this hull; inferred to mirror Coral Sul's 4x turbo-compression trains (see Coral South FLNG Terminal entry).
confirmed_how: TechnipFMC (EPCIC contractor) quoted in offshore-energy.biz (19 Dec 2025): 'We will leverage our experience gained from the successful delivery of Coral South — the world's first FLNG project in ultradeep water — by replicating our proven playbook with an enhanced approach.' Separately, offshore-energy.biz (16 Jan 2026) confirms the vessel 'Coral Norte FLNG' launch at Samsung Heavy's shipyard, Eni's second such unit after Coral Sul (delivered 2021), 432m x 66m, 123,000-tonne launch weight. Neither article gives Coral North's own turbine-vendor equipment list, so the captive-power finding here rests on documented design replication of an already-confirmed sister facility, not independent equipment confirmation for this hull.

hardware_summary: 4x turbo-compression trains (aeroderivative gas turbines driving centrifugal refrigeration compressors, mechanical drive) + 4x turbo-generation units (aeroderivative gas turbines driving GE Power Conversion electric generators), all supplied by Baker Hughes (a GE company)/BHGE Nuovo Pignone, assembled/tested at BHGE's Massa (Italy) facility; plus BOG/booster compressors down to -180°C.
fuel_basis: Feed/process gas from the Coral field liquefaction stream fuels the aeroderivative gas turbines; both the compression-drive and generation trains are gas turbines per the Baker Hughes contract announcements (2017).
captive_summary: Coral Sul FLNG (operating, Eni-operated, 3.4 Mtpa) carries on-board captive power: Baker Hughes/GE supplied 4 turbo-compression trains (mechanical drive for mixed-refrigeration compressors) plus 4 separate turbo-generation units in which aeroderivative gas turbines drive GE Power Conversion electric generators. This is both a mechanical-drive finding (True) and a genuine on-site electricity-generation finding (power_generation), so category is the mixed case.
mechanical_drive_note: 4x aeroderivative-gas-turbine-driven turbo-compression trains for mix-refrigeration service (Baker Hughes/BHGE Nuovo Pignone, per 2017 contract announcements); no aggregate shaft-power/MW figure disclosed in the sources found.
confirmed_how: offshore-energy.biz (31 Aug 2017, 'Baker Hughes in Another Coral South Win'): 'four turbo-compression trains for mix refrigeration services, using the company's aeroderivative gas turbine technology and driving its centrifugal compressors' and 'four turbo-generation units, also driven by aeroderivative gas turbines' with 'electric generators provided by the GE Power Conversion business.' Corroborated by a same-outlet companion article (30 Aug 2017, 'Baker Hughes secures another Coral South FLNG contract'): 'The order consists of four turbo-compression trains for mix refrigeration services and four turbo-generation units,' manufactured at 'BHGE Nuovo Pignone facility in Florence, Italy.' Both articles are the same publisher's coverage of the same underlying 2017 Baker Hughes contract announcement (treated as one effective source per the mirror rule), hence yellow rather than green; I could not find an independent second-publisher account or the original Baker Hughes/GE press release with a live/waybacked URL (Baker Hughes' own newsroom no longer lists 2017-era releases; nsenergybusiness.com and offshore-technology.com carry corroborating equipment detail including the PGT25+G4 turbine model, but both 403'd against url_verifier.py with no Wayback snapshot available, so neither is usable as a citation here).

hardware_summary: The FSRU itself is a regasification-only unit; it delivers regasified LNG to an adjacent, separately-owned Karpowership floating power plant (a 'Powership'), which is where the gas-fired generation actually sits.
fuel_basis: N/A — the terminal's own function is regasification, not generation; the adjacent Powership's generation is a different asset (Karpowership's, not this terminal's).
captive_summary: Nacala FSRU (KARMOL — a Mitsui O.S.K. Lines/Karpowership joint venture) is the LNG-supply half of Mozambique's first 'LNG-to-Powership' project: the FSRU regasifies LNG and delivers the gas to a separately-moored Karpowership Powership (previously running on heavy fuel oil), which burns it to generate ~120 MW for Mozambique's grid at Nacala. This is the textbook direction-test case: the terminal's whole purpose is supplying gas OUT to an external power station, not powering itself. Verdict is a documented NO for the terminal's own captive-power question; the relationship belongs in PowerPlantsSupplied for a different batch.
confirmed_how: offshore-energy.biz (2 Sep 2019, 'MOL, Karpowership Unveil 1st LNG-to-Powership Project in Africa'): 'the FSRU to deliver regasified LNG and the Powership to receive regasified LNG in order to produce electricity'; located at Nacala, Mozambique, where the Powership had been running on heavy fuel oil before the switch to LNG; combined capacity 120 MW, delivered under the co-brand 'Karmol' (MOL + Karpower International).
gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT prior 'Karpowership (Mozambique) Mehmet Bey power station' (125 MW, 2.5 km) is precisely the Powership vessel this FSRU feeds — it is NOT this terminal's own captive plant, it is the external generation asset the FSRU exists to supply. GOGPT's own gogpt_captive:'False' flag on that plant is consistent with it being a merchant/grid-feeding station rather than anyone's captive supply.
gogpt_candidate_basis: GOGPT record already exists for the Karpowership Powership itself (the actual generating asset); nothing new to add on the FSRU side, which has no generation of its own.
status_or_other_findings: GEM currently lists Nacala FSRU as shelved (inferred, ~2y). Owner: KARMOL [100%].
notes: PowerPlantsSupplied direction-test case: Nacala FSRU's entire purpose is feeding the Karpowership (Mozambique) Mehmet Bey Powership. Flagging for a PowerPlantsSupplied entry in a future Update batch (not staged here — out of scope for this captive-power pass).

hardware_summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries 120 MW dual-shaft H-100 gas turbines as mechanical drivers for the main liquefaction (refrigeration) compressors, supplied together with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Compressor (MCO) main liquefaction compressors, for Rovuma LNG Phase 1 (two trains, Air Products AP-X process, ≥7.6 Mtpa).
fuel_basis: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries H-100 gas turbines, natural-gas fuelled, named explicitly in the source as the mechanical drivers for the liquefaction trains.
captive_summary: The onshore Rovuma LNG project (Mozambique Rovuma Venture — the successor entity to the original ExxonMobil-led Area 4 onshore development, adjacent to but distinct from TotalEnergies' Mozambique LNG/Area 1 site) has a confirmed 2019 equipment order for Mitsubishi Heavy Industries 120 MW H-100 dual-shaft gas turbines as mechanical drivers for its liquefaction compressors — mechanical-drive captive gas power, which counts under the current definition regardless of the fact no separate electricity-generation figure was found.
mechanical_drive_note: MHI 120 MW dual-shaft H-100 gas turbines as mechanical drivers (2 trains per the Phase 1 scope described in the source); aggregate/per-train shaft-power breakdown beyond the 120 MW-class rating was not further specified.
confirmed_how: offshore-energy.biz (1 Apr 2019, 'Mitsubishi Heavy to supply equipment for Rovuma LNG project'): 'Japan's Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) has reached an agreement with ExxonMobil to supply a gas turbine and compressor packages for the Rovuma LNG Phase 1 project in Mozambique' — specifically '120 megawatt dual-shaft H-100 gas turbines as the mechanical drivers,' with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Compressor (MCO) supplying 'the main liquefaction compressors'; project scope described as two liquefaction trains, ≥7.6 Mtpa, using Air Products' AP-X process. Single-publisher source; I could not find a second, independently-published account of this specific 2019 MHI order in the time available.
gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT prior 'Mozambique LNG power station' (324 MW, 2.8 km) is the SGT-800 plant confirmed under the separate Mozambique LNG Terminal entry (T100000130257, this shard) — that plant belongs to the adjacent TotalEnergies-operated Area 1 project, a different industrial host, not to Rovuma LNG's own MRV-operated site. The captive-to-whom test says no: this is not Rovuma LNG's captive power.
gogpt_candidate_basis: The confirmed captive finding here is mechanical-drive shaft power (MHI H-100 turbines driving compressors directly), not an electricity-generating plant with a nameplate MW — GOGPT tracks electricity generation, so mechanical-drive-only equipment is not a GOGPT candidate on its own. No separate on-site generator finding was made for this project.
status_or_other_findings: GEM lists this project's units as 'T1-T12,' proposed, no year set — a far larger nominal unit count than the 'two liquefaction trains, >=7.6 Mtpa Phase 1' scope described in the 2019 MHI source; flagging the scale/train-count discrepancy for a future Update pass, not acted on here.
notes: Adjacent-but-distinct from Mozambique LNG Terminal (T100000130257) at the same Afungi/Cabo Delgado LNG park — see that entry's gogpt_prior_assessment for the reciprocal cross-reference.
